abstract: Prosocial helping is vital for reciprocal relationships. Deficits in prosocial helping behaviors are observed in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the causal relationship and molecular mechanisms driving these deficits remain poorly understood. Using a novel mouse model of the rescuable ASD-associated Nlgn3R451C mutation, we revealed severe deficits in helping behaviors that are not attributable to changes in sensory processing, cognition, emotional contagion, anxiety, social motivation, or motor ability. The helping deficits are linked to thalamic hypoactivation, dysregulation of inhibitory synaptic gene networks, and impaired inhibitory transmission in the mediodorsal thalamus (MD). Restoring endogenous NLGN3 expression in MD neurons and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) microdosing each partially rescued helping and concomitant inhibitory transmission deficits. Our work establishes a cause-and-effect relationship between a single ASD-associated gene and deficits in helping behaviors, reveals reduced thalamic inhibition as a potential underlying mechanism, and provides evidence that MDMA microdosing rescues these deficits, paving the way for treating helping deficits in individuals with ASD.
